objective: Compare four real model candidates as semantic worthiness assessors on a diagnostic adversarial bake-off.
finding: Gemini 3.8 Flash completed all four diagnostic cases; Gemini 3.8 Flash High completed one and timed out on three; Muse 1.2/1.3 failed JSON normalization on all four cases. The benchmark also exposed that current gold labels collapse contextual/historical/contradictory evidence into 'distractor', making exact semantic scoring too coarse.
decision: Do not declare a permanent semantic-assessor winner. Use ag/gemini-3.8-flash as the provisional treatment candidate for the next frozen benchmark, while improving the gold taxonomy and instrumenting Muse raw responses separately.
next_step: Expand worthiness gold taxonomy with direct_support, supporting, contextual, contradiction, obsolete/proposed labels.
Run a small fixed human/oracle audit on the same 4 cases.
Re-test Gemini 3.8 Flash on the expanded taxonomy.
Build a raw-response capture path for Muse so parse failures remain diagnosable.
Only then run the 16-case semantic treatment benchmark.
